rows.title: The Path of the First Breath
rows.summary: Path 11 joins Chokmah, Wisdom, to Kether, the Crown. It belongs to Aleph, the Ox, to elemental Air and to Atu 0, The Fool, and the Sepher Yetzirah calls it the Scintillating Intelligence. Working it builds openness, the willingness to begin without guarantees, and a lightness of spirit that is free rather than careless.
rows.prepare_incense: Galbanum (777 col. XLII perfume of path 11). Add a touch of musk, Chokmah's perfume, for the lower temple if you have it.
rows.prepare_candle: Bright pale yellow candle (King scale of Aleph) on a grey cloth (Queen scale of Chokmah). A sky-blue cloth (Queen scale of the path) is an alternative.
rows.prepare_stone: Topaz (777 col. XL)
rows.prepare_facing: East, the quarter of Air
rows.prepare_notes: Banish first, with the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram or Liber XXV (the Star Ruby). A dagger or a fan, the weapons of Air, can lie on the altar. A window opened a little lets real moving air into the room. The working relies on the breath, so keep the fourfold holds gentle and shorten them if you feel light-headed. Keep your diary and a pen within reach and set aside about 25 undisturbed minutes. This is a supernal path, above the Abyss. Many teachers advise knowing the lower paths well before working it, and treating what you see as symbolic contemplation rather than attainment.
rows.closing: Declare the working closed, then perform the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram or the Star Ruby. Stamp your foot firmly and put out the candle. Airy paths can leave you light-headed or scattered, so ground with care: eat something substantial (bread or something salty), drink water, and walk on the ground or hold something heavy for a minute. In your magical diary, record the date, time, moon phase, your physical and mental state, and everything you saw and received. Then check your record against the symbols list: note what matches and what does not, and force neither. Leave interpretation for a day or two.
rows.tunnel_reflection: In its averse aspect, the Fool's openness sinks into plain emptiness: freedom without direction, a leap that is only a fall, spirit scattering into vagueness, distraction or a refusal ever to commit. Consider the difference between an innocence that holds to nothing because it is whole and a drift that holds to nothing because it fears choosing. Treat Amprodias as a mirror for that difference, not as a force to call, and build up the day-side path of Aleph first.
rows.notes: Attributions follow Crowley's Thoth deck and Liber 777: Aleph, elemental Air, Atu 0 The Fool (777 title 'The Spirit of Aethyr'), joining Kether and Chokmah. The Golden Dawn also places the Fool on Aleph, so no swap applies here. The He/Tzaddi (Star/Emperor) exchange from Liber AL I:57 affects only paths 15 and 28. Data corrections: path 12's entries have run into the digest's plant, perfume and magical-power cells for this path. Standard 777 for path 11 is plants Aspen, perfume Galbanum, magical power Divination. 'Vervain, Herb Mercury, Major-lane [Marjolane], Palm [[Lime or', 'Mastic, White Sandal, [[Nutmeg]]' and 'Miracles of Healing, Gift of Tongues, Knowledge of [Sciences]' belong to path 12 and are not used here. The digest's tunnel 'power' field (Divination) is correct. The digest's 'correct design of the trump' entry ('a bearded Ancient seen in profile') echoes Kether's magical image. It may be Liber 777's own entry rather than a data error, but it does not describe the painted Thoth Atu 0. The veil and path therefore use the published Thoth imagery, and the Ancient appears only at the Kether threshold. The '[Swords] Emperors or Princes' note under the general Tarot attribution refers to the court cards of Air and is not an error. Optional: 777 col. V gives YHVH as the divine name of this path, which can be vibrated at the veil after Aleph. Chokmah's God-name Yah and archangel Ratziel follow the Golden Dawn and 777. The tunnel genius Amprodias comes from Liber 231 as used in Kenneth Grant's Nightside of Eden. The digest's Arabic-script spelling of the name is not traditional and was left out. This is a supernal path above the Abyss, so treat the journey as symbolic contemplation.

rows.title: The Path of the Winged Word
rows.summary: Path 12 joins Binah, Understanding, to Kether, the Crown. It belongs to Beth, the House, and to Mercury, shown in the Thoth deck as Atu I, The Magus, and the Sepher Yetzirah calls it the Intelligence of Transparency. Working it builds clear intent, care with speech and skill, and the ability to let the will pass through you without bending it.
rows.prepare_incense: Mastic, white sandalwood, mace or storax (777 col. XLII perfumes of path 12). Optionally add a pinch of myrrh, Binah's perfume, while you build the lower temple.
rows.prepare_candle: Yellow candle (King scale of path 12) on a black cloth (Queen scale of Binah). You can add a purple ribbon or cloth for the path's Queen-scale colour.
rows.prepare_stone: Opal or agate (777 col. XL)
rows.prepare_facing: East
rows.prepare_notes: Banish first, with the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram or Liber XXV (the Star Ruby). Wednesday, or a planetary hour of Mercury, suits this path. A wand or caduceus can lie on the altar. Keep your magical diary and a pen within reach and set aside about 25 undisturbed minutes. This is a supernal path, above the Abyss. Many teachers advise knowing the lower paths well before working it. Treat what you see as symbolic contemplation, not as attainment of the grades these paths stand for.
rows.closing: Declare the working closed, then perform the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram or the Star Ruby. Stamp your foot firmly (three times, if that is your custom) and put out the candle. Eat something plain and substantial and drink some water. In your magical diary, record the date, time, moon phase, your physical and mental state, and everything you saw and received. Then check your record against the symbols list: note what matches and what does not, and force neither. Leave interpretation for a day or two.
rows.tunnel_reflection: Consider the Magus's shadow. The same quickness that carries truth can carry a lie, and the ape at his feet repeats the word without understanding it. Ask where your own cleverness has been used to mislead others or yourself, and where your speech has run ahead of the truth. Treat Baratchial as a mirror for this self-examination, not as a power to call, and work the day-side path of Beth until its clarity is steady before you turn to the tunnel.
rows.notes: Attributions follow Crowley's Thoth deck and Liber 777: Beth, Mercury, Atu I The Magus (777 title 'The Magus of Power'), joining Kether and Binah. The Golden Dawn places the Magician (Juggler) on this path too, so no swap applies here. The He/Tzaddi (Star/Emperor) exchange from Liber AL I:57 affects only paths 15 and 28. Data corrections: the digest's plant, perfume and magical-power cells are shifted by one row. Path 12's own values begin in path 11's cells, and path 12's cells hold the last words of its own entries followed by path 13 (Gimel/Moon) values: 'Almond, Mugwort, Hazel, Moonwort', 'Menstrual Blood, Camphor, Aloes' and 'The White Tincture, Clairvoyance, Divination by [Dreams]'. The journey uses the standard 777 values for path 12 instead. Plants: Vervain, Herb Mercury, Marjolane (marjoram), Palm, with the bracketed addition [[Lime or Linden]], which the shift split across the path 11 and 12 cells. Perfumes: Mastic, White Sandal, [[Nutmeg]], Mace, Storax, all fugitive odours. Powers: Miracles of Healing, Gift of Tongues, Knowledge of Sciences; the digest's tunnel 'power' field already has these correctly. Stone: 777 col. XL gives Opal, Agate for this path. 'Especially Fire Opal' is 777's qualifier for Hod's opal, so it is not given here. 'Helment' in the trump-design entry is a typo for helmet. Optional: 777 col. V gives this path the divine name Azbogah (אזבוגה, the 'name of eight', matching Mercury's number), which can be vibrated at the veil after Beth. Binah's God-name YHVH Elohim and archangel Tzaphkiel follow the Golden Dawn and 777. The tunnel genius Baratchial comes from Liber 231 as used in Kenneth Grant's Nightside of Eden. The digest's Arabic-script spelling of the name is not traditional and was left out. This is a supernal path above the Abyss, so treat the journey as symbolic contemplation.

rows.title: The Silver Road of the Priestess
rows.summary: Path 13, Gimel, runs straight up the Middle Pillar from Tiphareth through the Abyss to Kether. It is the longest path on the Tree, the path of the Moon and Atu II The Priestess. Working it develops stillness, receptivity and deep intuitive memory: the ability to become a clear, reflecting surface for what lies beyond the self.
rows.prepare_incense: Camphor (sparingly, as the smoke is sharp) or aloes wood (777 col. XLII: camphor, aloes, all sweet virginal odours). A grain of olibanum at the opening honours Tiphareth.
rows.prepare_candle: Blue, the path's King-scale colour (777 col. XV), on a silver or pale grey cloth for its Queen-scale silver (col. XVI). A gold candle or cloth for the Tiphareth opening is optional.
rows.prepare_stone: Moonstone, pearl or clear quartz crystal (777 col. XL)
rows.prepare_facing: East; if you work at night with the Moon visible, you may face the Moon instead
rows.prepare_notes: Work it on a Monday, in a planetary hour of the Moon, or near the full Moon. This is the highest path on the Middle Pillar and it crosses the Abyss, so tradition has it worked late, after the lower paths and the paths into Tiphareth. Dim light is enough. Keep your diary within reach, because lunar impressions fade like dreams. The holds add up to about 15 minutes; allow 20 to 25 minutes in all.
rows.closing: Banish with the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram or the Star Ruby. Stamp your feet, then eat something substantial and drink water, because lunar work can leave you dreamy and ungrounded. Record the session in your diary: date, time, planetary hour, Moon phase, what you saw, and the guide's word or symbol. Then check it against the symbols list, noting what matched and what did not. For the next few nights, keep a dream log. 777 gives divination by dreams as this path's magical power, and material from the working often surfaces there.
rows.tunnel_reflection: On the averse side, the Priestess's veil hardens into a wall: secrecy kept for its own sake, a Moon that reflects nothing, dream-fog and psychic glamour mistaken for depth, memory circling on itself among ghosts. In plain waking reflection, consider where you hoard the hidden to feel special, or prefer vague impressions to clear seeing. Work the day-side path of Gimel first, and more than once. Keep this as contemplation and journaling, not a journey into the tunnel.
rows.notes:
Attributions follow Liber 777 and The Book of Thoth. Path 13 is not affected by Crowley's Tzaddi/He swap; the Moon and Atu II are the same in the Golden Dawn and Thoth systems. Crowley titles the card 'The Priestess', and its Book T title is 'The Priestess of the Silver Star'.

Where the digest was incomplete or differed:
- Plants: the digest listed only ranunculus. 777 col. XXXIX gives almond, mugwort, hazel (as Luna), moonwort and ranunculus, and these are used.
- Perfumes: the digest gave only 'sweet virginal odours'. 777 col. XLII also lists camphor and aloes.
- Magical powers: the digest's main field said only 'Dreams'. 777 col. XLV gives the White Tincture, clairvoyance and divination by dreams, as the digest's tunnel field correctly shows.
- Trump design: the digest's 'correct design' line (a crowned priestess before the veil of Isis, between the Pillars of Seth) is the older Golden Dawn description. The steps follow Crowley's painted Thoth design.
- Tiphareth's vision: the digest's field was truncated. It is 'the Vision of the Harmony of Things (also the Mysteries of the Crucifixion)'.

Other notes:
- Tiphareth's archangel follows the 777 / Golden Dawn order given for this project (Raphael); some systems give Michael.
- Path 13 crosses the Abyss and Daath. In Thelemic terms, visualising it rehearses the path's symbols; it is not the crossing the A∴A∴ treats as a grade attainment. Keep the approach to Kether a brief, modest glimpse.

rows.title: The Door of the Empress
rows.summary: Path 14, Daleth, runs level across the top of the Tree between Binah and Chokmah, joining Understanding and Wisdom above the Abyss. It is the path of Venus and Atu III The Empress, the 'door' where the Father's force and the Mother's form meet. Working it develops love as a creative principle: the fertile imagination that gives birth to form, and a felt sense that the supernal pair are one.
rows.prepare_incense: Sandalwood, myrtle or rose (777 col. XLII: sandalwood, myrtle, all soft voluptuous odours). A pinch of myrrh at the opening honours the Binah temple.
rows.prepare_candle: Emerald green, the path's King-scale colour (777 col. XV), on a sky-blue cloth, its Queen-scale colour (col. XVI). A black cloth under the candle for Binah's Queen-scale colour is optional.
rows.prepare_stone: Emerald or turquoise (777 col. XL)
rows.prepare_facing: East, the usual quarter for temple work
rows.prepare_notes: Work it on a Friday or in a planetary hour of Venus. Path 14 is a supernal path, so tradition has it worked after the lower paths. Keep the light low and the room warm. Have your diary and the symbols checklist ready. The holds add up to about 15 minutes; with reading time, allow 20 to 25 minutes.
rows.closing: Banish with the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram, or the Star Ruby if that is your practice. Stamp your feet or press them firmly into the floor, then eat something simple, such as bread or fruit, and drink water. Record the session in your magical diary: date, time, planetary hour, Moon phase, what you saw, and the guide's word or symbol. Then check it against the symbols list, noting what matched, what did not, and anything new. Leave interpretation for a day or two.
rows.tunnel_reflection: On the averse side, the door of Daleth opens only inward. Love narrows into appetite, and the fertile mother becomes one who devours what she bears: the pelican reversed, feeding on her young instead of feeding them. In ordinary waking reflection, consider where your desire seeks to possess rather than to create, and where care has turned into control. Work the day-side path of the Empress several times first, and keep this as notebook contemplation, not a journey or an invocation.
rows.notes:
Attributions follow Liber 777 and The Book of Thoth. Path 14 is not affected by Crowley's Tzaddi/He swap; Venus and Atu III are the same in the Golden Dawn and Thoth systems.

Corrections to the digest:
- The 'Title of the Tarot trump' field ran into the next row. The fragment 'The Son of the Morning, chief among the [Mighty]' (often printed 'Sun of the Morning, Chief among the Mighty') is the Book T title of Atu IV The Emperor. The Empress's title is 'The Daughter of the Mighty Ones'.
- The 'correct design' line in the digest (a winged, star-crowned goddess standing on the Moon) appears to be the older Golden Dawn-style description, not the painted Thoth card. The steps follow Crowley's Thoth design.

Other notes:
- Binah's magical image here is 'a mature woman, a matron', from Golden Dawn usage. 777 remarks that almost any female image shows some aspect of Binah.
- Path 14 is horizontal, so 'lower' and 'upper' are conventions. It is worked here from Binah (3) to Chokmah (2), but can equally be worked from Chokmah.
- The Sepher Yetzirah title is sometimes translated 'Luminous Intelligence'.
- The swan and the wider 'birds' entry appear in the digest as bracketed secondary animals.

rows.title: The Window of the Star
rows.summary: The fifteenth path, He (the window), rises from Tiphareth, the solar centre of the Adept, across the Abyss to Chokmah, the sphere of the fixed stars. In Crowley's arrangement it carries Atu XVII, The Star, and Aquarius: Nuit pouring the waters of life, and the recognition of oneself as a star in the body of infinite space. Working it develops clear aspiration, hope grounded in perception rather than fantasy, and a felt sense of one's own orbit.
rows.prepare_incense: Galbanum (777 col. XLII, Aquarius row, which follows the Star under Crowley's swap). A little olibanum may be burned first for the temple of Tiphareth. (Golden Dawn attribution: dragon's blood, for Aries.)
rows.prepare_candle: A violet candle (King scale of Aquarius, 777 col. XV) on a sky-blue cloth (Queen scale, col. XVI); a gold or yellow candle may stand for Tiphareth. (Golden Dawn / 777 as first printed for path 15: scarlet.)
rows.prepare_stone: Chalcedony, or a clear glass sphere (777 col. XL: artificial glass).
rows.prepare_facing: East, the quarter of Air for fixed-air Aquarius and the station of Raphael.
rows.prepare_notes: Saturday (Saturn is the traditional ruler of Aquarius) or any clear night; if you can, spend a few minutes looking at the real night sky before you begin. Study the Thoth Atu XVII before closing your eyes. Banish beforehand; the Star Ruby is especially fitting. Have your record ready. This path crosses the Abyss, and the journey halts at its edge by design.
rows.closing: Perform a banishing: the Star Ruby suits this path well, or use the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram. Stamp your feet, drink a glass of water, and eat something simple; if you feel light-headed or elated, a short walk outdoors helps. Record the session: date, time, sky conditions, what you saw, the Star's answer and anything received. Test the vision against the symbol list, noting matches, misses, and anything that belongs to the Golden Dawn Emperor/Aries set instead (ram, scarlet, ruby), which shows which attribution your imagination is drawing on. Revisit the notes after a day or two before interpreting them.
rows.tunnel_reflection: The averse face of the Window is a pane that, turned toward the dark, shows only your own reflection: hope become fantasy, a star followed because it flatters, visions consecrated that lead nowhere. Consider, as reflection and not invocation, where your aspiration has become a picture you gaze at instead of a direction you travel, and where borrowed light has been mistaken for your own. Work the day-side path of the Star until it is familiar before turning to this, and banish afterwards.
rows.notes: Crowley's swap: following Liber AL I:57 ('but צ [Tzaddi] is not the Star'), Crowley exchanged Atu IV and Atu XVII. In the Thoth system path 15 (He, Tiphareth to Chokmah) carries Atu XVII The Star with Aquarius, and path 28 (Tzaddi, Netzach to Yesod) carries Atu IV The Emperor with Aries. The Golden Dawn attribution, and 777's row for path 15 as printed, is He = The Emperor = Aries. The digest supplied that Emperor/Aries set: the trump, scarlet/red/brilliant flame/glowing red, ram and owl, tiger lily and geranium, ruby, dragon's blood, Men Thu, Athena, Mars and Minerva, the power of consecrating things, the fragment 'Mighty' (from the Emperor's title 'Sun of the Morning, Chief among the Mighty'), and the Emperor's 'correct design' (a flame-clad god). This journey replaces it with the Aquarian correspondences that travel with the Star, taken from 777's Aquarius row (path 28): violet, sky blue, bluish mauve, white tinged purple; man or eagle (Cherub of Air) and peacock; olive and coconut; artificial glass and chalcedony; galbanum; censer or aspergillus; Ganymede and Juno; power: astrology. The trump title becomes 'The Daughter of the Firmament, the Dweller between the Waters'. Crowley did not reissue 777's colour and correspondence rows after the swap, so carrying the whole Aquarius set to path 15 is a common Thoth-based reading rather than a printed table; some practitioners keep 777's scarlet on path 15 regardless of the swap. If you work Golden Dawn style, use the Emperor, scarlet and Aries throughout. The letter meaning (window) and the Sepher Yetzirah Intelligence (Constituting) belong to the path and do not move. Also corrected: the digest's magical-weapon field ran on into path 16 ('The Labour of Preparation' belongs to Vau), so only 'the horns, energy, the burin' is the Aries entry. The tunnel entry's power ('consecrating things') is likewise the Aries value. This path crosses the Abyss, so the journey halts at its edge and looks across; Chokmah is shown in its 777 colours (grey, pure soft blue, pearl iridescence). Crowley's identification of the Star figure as Nuit is followed; the paraphrased phrase 'every man and every woman is a star' is Liber AL I:3. Card details are paraphrased, and the glass sphere, censer on the branch and window framing are visualisation devices, not traditional teaching.

rows.title: The Path of the Nail
rows.summary: The sixteenth path, Vau (the nail), rises from Chesed, Mercy, across the Abyss to Chokmah, Wisdom. Under Taurus and Atu V, The Hierophant, it is the path of revelation: the nail that joins the divine to the human, and the teaching heard as an inner voice rather than received as an outer rule. Working it develops steadiness, patient inner listening, and the discernment to tell living tradition from dead dogma.
rows.prepare_incense: Storax (777 col. XLII, Taurus). A pinch of cedar may be burned first for the temple of Chesed.
rows.prepare_candle: A red-orange candle (King scale of the path, 777 col. XV) on a deep indigo cloth (Queen scale, col. XVI). A blue candle may stand for the temple of Chesed (its Queen-scale colour).
rows.prepare_stone: Topaz (777 col. XL), held in the hand or set before you.
rows.prepare_facing: North, the quarter of Earth, for fixed-earth Taurus. East is fine if you face East for all path work.
rows.prepare_notes: Friday or an hour of Venus suits Taurus, which Venus rules. Study the Thoth Atu V for a few minutes before closing your eyes. Banish beforehand (Star Ruby or LBRP). Have your record and a pen ready. This path crosses the Abyss: approach it as an act of listening, go no farther than the journey describes, and do not repeat it on the same day.
rows.closing: Perform a banishing: the Star Ruby or the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram. Stamp your feet, drink water, and eat something plain and earthy such as bread or root vegetables. Write the session into your magical record: date, time, planetary day and hour, what you saw and heard, the Hierophant's answer, and anything you were given. Then check your notes against the symbol list, marking what matched, what did not, and what surprised you. Leave interpretation for a day or two, and do not repeat the working on the same day.
rows.tunnel_reflection: The averse face of Vau is the nail that fixes instead of joins: teaching hardened into dogma, ritual performed with no one listening, authority that demands obedience instead of awakening understanding. Consider, as reflection and not invocation, where your own practice has set like a driven nail: beliefs you no longer test, voices you defer to in place of your own inner hearing. Work the day-side path of the Hierophant first, and more than once, before sitting with this; contemplate it from a steady footing and banish afterwards.
rows.notes: Attributions follow Crowley's Thoth tarot and Liber 777: Vau, Taurus, Atu V The Hierophant. Path 16 is not affected by the He/Tzaddi swap. This path crosses the Abyss (Chesed to Chokmah), so the journey stops at the first nail of the bridge and glimpses Chokmah across the gulf instead of approaching its temple; treat it as an act of listening, not a claim to any grade. Chokmah's glimpse uses its 777 colours: grey (Queen), pure soft blue (King), pearl-grey iridescence (Emperor). Digest corrections (the source table had rows bleeding in from path 17, Gemini): Greek gods: 777 gives only (Hera) for Taurus; 'Castor and Pollux, Apollo the Diviner' belong to path 17. Trump title: 'The Magus of the Eternal'; 'The Children of the Voice: the Oracle of the Mighty Gods' is the title of Atu VI, The Lovers (path 17). Magical power: 'The Secret of Physical Strength'; the power of being in two or more places at once, and of prophecy, belongs to path 17. Magical weapon: 'The Labour of Preparation (the Throne and Altar)'; its first half had slipped into path 15's row in the digest. The 'correct design' field is truncated: 777 describes an Ancient between the pillars, crowned, sceptred and blessing threefold, adored by four living creatures. Thoth-card details are paraphrased from the Harris painting. The gate, the topaz in the gatepost and the nailed bridge are visualisation devices, not traditional teaching.

rows.title: The Path of the Oracle
rows.summary: The seventeenth path runs from Tiphareth, the solar centre of the Tree, across the Abyss to Binah. It is attributed to Zain (the sword), to Gemini and to Atu VI The Lovers. Working it develops discrimination and union together: the ability to divide things clearly, to hold two opposites without collapsing either one, and to let a true answer emerge where they meet.
rows.prepare_incense: Wormwood (777 col. XLII). Burn only a small pinch on charcoal, because the smoke is harsh, and ventilate the room afterwards. Olibanum (frankincense), the perfume of Tiphareth, is a gentler companion or substitute.
rows.prepare_candle: An orange candle (the King scale of Zain) on a pale mauve cloth (the Queen scale of Zain). Two candles side by side suit Gemini if you like.
rows.prepare_stone: Iceland spar (clear optical calcite, which doubles whatever you see through it), tourmaline or alexandrite (777 col. XL). Hold it in your left hand or set it on the altar in front of you.
rows.prepare_facing: East. Golden Dawn practice gives East to Air, and Gemini is an Air sign. East is also the quarter of the rising sun of Tiphareth.
rows.prepare_notes: Wednesday is a good day (Mercury rules Gemini), as is any time the Moon is in Gemini. A small tripod or three-legged stand holding the stone or the incense echoes the path's weapon. Work seated upright. This path crosses the Abyss to Binah, so the script stops at the threshold and does not enter. Keep your journal ready, and write before you check the correspondences.
rows.closing: Perform the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram, or Liber XXV (the Star Ruby) if that is your practice. Stamp your feet firmly, drink water and eat something simple. Put out the candle and air the room of wormwood smoke. Write the record straight away: date, time, the Moon's sign, what you saw, heard and felt, and any word or symbol you received. Only then compare it with the symbol list, marking what matches the correspondences and what does not. Over the next few days, notice any choices or pairings that come up and add them to the record.
rows.tunnel_reflection: In Grant's Nightside scheme, Zamradiel holds the seventeenth tunnel. Its averse face is division for its own sake: the sword that only cuts apart, the broken union, the mind that weighs every pair of options until it can choose neither, the twin who turns on the other. Consider where your own discrimination has become endless splitting or indecision, and what it would take for the sword to serve a union instead of preventing one. Treat this as reflection, not invocation, and work the day-side path until it is familiar before you turn toward its shadow.
rows.notes: Attribution: Crowley and the Golden Dawn agree on this path: Zain, Gemini, Atu VI The Lovers, path 17 joining Tiphareth (6) and Binah (3). The He/Tzaddi swap does not affect it. Crowley heads the card 'The Lovers (or The Brothers)' and pairs it with Atu XIV Art, with the marriage here and its consummation there. Corrections to the digest, which had shifted rows: (1) The trump title field held a fragment of Atu VII's title. The title of Atu VI is 'The Children of the Voice: the Oracle of the Mighty Gods'. (2) The animals field mixed in Cheth's creatures (Crab, Turtle, Sphinx, Whale), which belong to path 18. The 777 animals for Zain are Magpie and hybrids [Parrot, Zebra, Penguin]. (3) The Greek gods field was truncated. The full entry is Castor and Pollux, Apollo the Diviner [Eros]. (4) Magical powers: 777 gives 'Being in two or more places at one time' as well as Prophecy. (5) Tiphareth's vision field was cut short. It is the Vision of the Harmony of Things (Mysteries of the Crucifixion) [Beatific Vision]. Other points: this path crosses the Abyss, so the journey only glimpses Binah from the threshold. Alternative guides are Apollo the Diviner or the twins Castor and Pollux. The tunnel genius name comes from the Qliphothic genii of Crowley's Liber 231, as Grant uses them.

rows.title: The Path of the Grail-Bearer
rows.summary: The eighteenth path joins Geburah, the sphere of Mars and Severity, to Binah, the Great Mother beyond the Abyss. It is attributed to Cheth (the fence), to Cancer and to Atu VII The Chariot. Working it builds the discipline of the vessel: a self that is armoured and ordered so that it can carry something holy without spilling it, not so that it can conquer.
rows.prepare_incense: Onycha, the path perfume in 777 col. XLII. Benzoin or storax are the usual practical substitutes. If you want to mark the starting sphere, burn a pinch of tobacco (777's perfume for Geburah) before you begin.
rows.prepare_candle: An amber candle (the King scale of Cheth) on a maroon cloth (the Queen scale of Cheth). You can add a scarlet candle (the Queen scale of Geburah) for the starting temple.
rows.prepare_stone: A piece of amber (777 col. XL). Hold it in your left hand or set it on the altar in front of you.
rows.prepare_facing: West. Golden Dawn practice gives West to Water, and Cancer is a Water sign.
rows.prepare_notes: Monday is a good day (the Moon rules Cancer), as is any time the Moon is in Cancer. A cup of water on the altar echoes the Grail. Work seated upright, not lying down. This path crosses the Abyss to Binah, so the script stops at the threshold and does not enter. Keep your journal within reach, and write up the vision before you look at the symbol list.
rows.closing: Perform the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram, or Liber XXV (the Star Ruby) if that is your practice. Stamp your feet firmly, drink a glass of water and eat something plain. Snuff the candle and put the amber away somewhere apart from everyday things. Write the record straight away: date, time, the Moon's sign, what you saw, heard and felt, and any word or symbol you received. Only then compare it with the symbol list, marking what matches the correspondences, what does not, and what surprised you.
rows.tunnel_reflection: In Kenneth Grant's Nightside scheme, Characith holds the eighteenth tunnel. Its averse face is the vehicle without a driver: momentum with no one at the centre, armour that has grown into a prison, and the power of casting enchantments turned inward as self-enchantment. Consider where your own discipline has become a shell that keeps life out instead of a vessel that carries it. Treat this as reflection, not invocation, and work the day-side path until it is familiar before you turn toward its shadow.
rows.notes: Attribution: Crowley and the Golden Dawn agree on this path: Cheth, Cancer, Atu VII The Chariot, path 18 joining Geburah (5) and Binah (3). The He/Tzaddi swap does not affect it. Corrections to the digest, which had shifted rows: (1) The Sepher Yetzirah field ran path 19 into path 18. The eighteenth path is only the Intelligence of the House of Influence; the Intelligence of all the Activities of the Spiritual Beings belongs to Teth. (2) The animals field held Teth's creatures (lion, cat, tiger, serpent). The 777 animals for Cheth are Crab, Turtle, Sphinx [Whale, all Beasts of Transport], and they had drifted into path 17's row. (3) The magical weapons field included Teth's Discipline (Preliminary) and Phoenix. Cheth's weapons are the Furnace [Cup or Holy Graal]. (4) The trump title was truncated. The full title is 'The Child of the Powers of the Waters: the Lord of the Triumph of Light', and its first half had slipped into path 17's row. (5) Geburah's vision field ran into Tiphareth's. Geburah's is the Vision of Power. Other points: this path crosses the Abyss, so the journey only glimpses Binah from the threshold. Alternative guide god-forms from 777 are Khephra and Apollo the Charioteer. The tunnel genius name comes from the Qliphothic genii of Crowley's Liber 231, as Grant uses them. 418 as the full spelling of Cheth is Crowley's own gematria, not Golden Dawn doctrine.

rows.title: The Path of the Lion and the Cup
rows.summary: Path 19 runs level across the Tree from Geburah (Mars, Severity) to Chesed (Jupiter, Mercy), through Teth the serpent, Leo, and Crowley's Atu XI Lust. It reconciles force and grace. Working it develops courage felt as joy, and the skill of guiding vital, animal energy through love rather than suppression.
rows.prepare_incense: Olibanum (frankincense), the 777 col. XLII perfume of path 19. A pinch of tobacco, 777's perfume for Geburah, is optional for the Geburah temple.
rows.prepare_candle: A greenish-yellow candle (King scale of path 19) on a deep purple cloth (Queen scale of path 19). A scarlet candle for Geburah (its Queen scale) is optional.
rows.prepare_stone: Cat's eye
rows.prepare_facing: South, because Leo is fixed Fire. East, the usual temple orientation, also works.
rows.prepare_notes: Work on a Sunday or in an hour of the Sun (Leo's ruler). Come to it rested and fed, not hungry or agitated, because this path stirs vitality and appetite. Banish first (LBRP or Star Ruby). Put a sunflower on the altar if one is in season, and keep a glass of water within reach. Keep the journal and the symbols checklist nearby, but don't read the checklist until afterwards. Allow 30-40 minutes, including reading time.
rows.closing: Close with the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram (or the Star Ruby), then stamp firmly on the floor to mark the end. Drink water and eat something substantial. If you feel charged or restless, take a short walk before you sit down to write. Journal straight away: date, time, conditions, the full sequence of images, how the lion behaved, the guide's form, and the word or gift you received. Then compare your record with the symbols list (what agrees, what is missing, what surprised you) without bending the vision to fit. Over the next day, notice any heat, desire, anger or elation. Effects of this path often show up in mood and appetite, and observing them is part of the training.
rows.tunnel_reflection: Reversed, this path is appetite with no rider: the lion let loose, an ecstasy that devours instead of illuminating, force that mistakes itself for freedom. As a reflection, not an invocation, consider where passion drives you rather than being ridden with love, and where suppressing it has only made the beast hungrier. Work the day-side path of Teth first, and approach the Tunnel of Temphioth only as a meditation on that shadow.
rows.notes: Thoth numbering: in Crowley's deck this trump is Atu XI Lust. The Golden Dawn and Waite call it VIII Strength. The Golden Dawn had moved Strength to VIII and Justice to XI so that the trumps follow the order of the letters. Crowley went back to the older Marseille numbering (XI Lust, VIII Adjustment) and kept Teth/Leo on Lust and Lamed/Libra on Adjustment. Unlike the He/Tzaddi swap on paths 15 and 28, this exchange does not change the path attribution: Teth, Leo, Geburah to Chesed, exactly as in the Golden Dawn. The digest's 'atu: VIII' is corrected to XI for the Thoth deck; the digest's tunnel record already reads 'XI Lust'. Corrections to the digest: (1) The trump title is only 'The Daughter of the Flaming Sword'. The rest of that field ('The Prophet of the Eternal, the Magus of the...') belongs to Atu IX, path 20. (2) The 'Correct design' text (a smiling woman holding a lion's jaws) is 777's Golden Dawn image. The journey uses the Crowley-Harris Thoth design: the Woman riding the many-headed Beast and holding up the Graal. (3) The Sepher Yetzirah field was cut short to 'Being'; it is restored as the Intelligence of the Secret of all Spiritual Activities (Westcott: of all the activities of the spiritual beings). (4) The animals field ('Woman]]') and magical weapons field ('Wand]]') are truncated. 777 gives Lion (Kerub of Fire) for animals and 'The Discipline (Preliminary)' for weapons; the lion was used. (5) Geburah's vision field has text shifted in from Tiphareth. Geburah's vision is The Vision of Power; 'the Vision of the Harmony of Things' belongs to Tiphareth. The digest's 'Legendary orders of being' entry could not be verified and was not used. Everything else was used as given: colours, Ra-Hoor-Khuit/Pasht/Sekhet/Mau, Horus, Narasimha, Demeter, sunflower, cat's eye, olibanum, and the power of training wild beasts. Kamael is spelled כמאל as in the Golden Dawn. Tunnel genius Temphioth is from Grant's Nightside of Eden, after Liber 231.

rows.title: The Path of the Hidden Lamp
rows.summary: Path 20 joins Tiphareth, the solar heart of the Tree, to Chesed, the throne of Jupiter, through Yod, the hand and the seed-point of the Name, under Virgo and Atu IX The Hermit. The Sepher Yetzirah calls it the Intelligence of Will. Working it teaches the self-contained inner light, and develops solitude without isolation, discretion, and the patience of a seed carried through to its harvest.
rows.prepare_incense: Narcissus (777 col. XLII, the perfume of path 20). Olibanum may also be lit for the Tiphareth temple.
rows.prepare_candle: A yellowish-green candle (King scale of path 20) on a slate-grey cloth (Queen scale of path 20). A gold candle for Tiphareth (its Queen scale) is optional.
rows.prepare_stone: Peridot
rows.prepare_facing: East, the usual direction for temple work. Some prefer North because Virgo is an Earth sign.
rows.prepare_notes: Work in the evening, ideally on a Wednesday or in an hour of Mercury (Virgo's ruler). Banish first (LBRP or Star Ruby). Keep the room silent, since this path belongs to Harpocrates, the god of silence. Put a small piece of bread on the altar to eat at the close (777 lists the Bread among the path's weapons). Keep the journal and the symbols checklist nearby, but don't read the checklist until afterwards. Allow 30-40 minutes, including reading time.
rows.closing: Close with the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram (or the Star Ruby), then stamp once, firmly, on the floor to mark the end. Eat the bread from the altar, or something plain, and drink water. Put out the candle deliberately. Journal straight away, before interpreting anything: date, time, conditions, the whole sequence of images, the guide's form, and the word or gift you received. Then check your record against the symbols list. Note what agrees, what is missing and what is unexpected, but do not change the vision to make it fit. Leave at least a day before working another path, and keep the guide's word in mind as you go about the next day.
rows.tunnel_reflection: On its averse side, the Hermit's solitude hardens into isolation. The lamp is hoarded, the seed is held back until it withers, and discretion turns into secrecy for its own sake. As a reflection, and never as an evocation, consider where your own withdrawal has stopped nourishing anything and has become a wall. Work and journal the day-side path of Yod first, and then approach the Tunnel of Yamatu only as a meditation on that shadow, not as a journey into it.
rows.notes: Thoth and Golden Dawn agree on this path: Yod, Virgo, Atu IX The Hermit, Tiphareth to Chesed. The He/Tzaddi swap (paths 15 and 28) does not affect it. Corrections to the digest: (1) The 'Correct design of the Tarot trump' field runs on into the Atu X description ('A wheel of six shafts...'). That text belongs to path 21 and was left out. (2) The trump title is cut short. 777 gives 'The Prophet of the Eternal, the Magus of the Voice of Power'; the first half of that title slipped into the path 19 record. (3) Tiphareth's vision field is scrambled by a shifted row. The standard entry is 'The Vision of the Harmony of Things (also the Mysteries of the Crucifixion)', with the Beatific Vision as Crowley's addition; the first half was found under Geburah in the path 19 digest. (4) The col. V divine-name entry ('(34) אל אב (4) אבא') is not garbled. It reads El Ab, 'God the Father' (gematria 34), and Abba, 'Father' (gematria 4), which fits Yod as the Father-letter of YHVH. It is a correspondence for contemplation, not a name for vibration, so the journey vibrates only the Tiphareth God-name and the letter name. Everything else in the digest agrees with 777 and was used: colours, Sepher Yetzirah 'Intelligence of Will', Isis as Virgin, Heru-pa-kraath, plants, peridot, narcissus, lamp/wand/bread, invisibility and parthenogenesis. Heru-pa-kraath (Harpocrates) is offered as an alternative form for the guide. The Tiphareth and Chesed temples use their Queen-scale colours. The Crowley-Harris Thoth design (lamp holding a sun, Orphic egg, Cerberus, wheat) replaces 777's older Golden Dawn description. Tunnel genius Yamatu is from Grant's Nightside of Eden, after Liber 231.

rows.title: The Path of the Turning Wheel
rows.summary: Path 21 runs from Netzach, the green sphere of Venus, to Chesed, the blue sphere of Jupiter. It falls under the letter Kaph (the palm), the planet Jupiter and Atu X Fortune. Working it builds the ability to meet change and expansion without clutching. You learn to see rising and falling circumstance as a rhythm, and to find the still hub within it where grace and opportunity can be received.
rows.prepare_incense: Saffron (777 col. XLII: saffron and all generous odours). Cedar suits the Chesed threshold, and a little benzoin or rose may be burned at the Netzach opening.
rows.prepare_candle: A violet candle (King scale of path 21) on a blue cloth (Queen scale of path 21). An emerald-green candle for the Netzach temple (its Queen scale) is optional.
rows.prepare_stone: Amethyst or lapis lazuli (777 col. XL).
rows.prepare_facing: East, the usual quarter for opening path work. If you know where Jupiter is in the sky, you may face it instead.
rows.prepare_notes: Best on a Thursday or in an hour of Jupiter. Banish first (LBRP or Star Ruby) and do the Qabalistic Cross. The journey starts in Netzach, so prior work on the paths that reach it (29, 28, 27) helps make the temple vivid. Study the Thoth Atu X Fortune for a few minutes before closing your eyes. Keep your diary within reach.
rows.closing: Once you are back in the room, perform the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram (or the Star Ruby) and seal with the Qabalistic Cross. Stamp your feet, drink water and eat something simple and grounding. In your magical diary, record the date, time, planetary hour and the Moon's sign, the guide's word or symbol, and everything you met on the path. Then check it against the symbol list. Mark what matched, what did not, and anything that felt invented rather than received. Come back to the entry after a day or two before drawing conclusions.
rows.tunnel_reflection: In its averse aspect the wheel becomes a cage. Fortune is felt as something that merely happens to you, rising and falling with no lesson, and Jupiter's expansion swells into a hunger for ascendancy for its own sake. Consider where you have handed your will over to luck, or clung to a rise as though it could never turn. Treat this as reflection, not invocation. Work the day-side path of Fortune first, so the still hub is familiar before you look at the rim from below.
rows.notes: Thoth attribution: Kaph, Jupiter, Atu X Fortune ('Wheel of Fortune' in the Golden Dawn). No swap or renumbering affects this path. Corrections to the digest: (1) Trump title: 777 gives 'The Lord of the Forces of Life'. The trailing 'The Daughter of the Lords of Truth...' belongs to Atu VIII (path 22) and shifted in from the next row. (2) Greek gods: 777 gives Zeus for Kaph. 'Themis, Minos, Aeacus and [Rhadamanthus]' belongs to Lamed (path 22). (3) Archangel: the digest spells Haniel האניאל, with an extra Aleph. The usual Golden Dawn spelling, הניאל, is used here. (4) The digest's 'Legendary orders of being' entry (Incubi, Nightmares) could not be confirmed against 777, so it is left out of the symbol list. Kaph's value is 20, and its final form ך is 500. The Sepher Yetzirah title is usually rendered 'Intelligence of Conciliation and Reward', and its text is paraphrased here. Netzach's God-name is YHVH Tzabaoth; Elohim Tzabaoth belongs to Hod. Assigning Sulphur, Mercury and Salt to the Sphinx, Hermanubis and Typhon follows Crowley's account of the card. Amoun-Ra is 777's Egyptian attribution. The description of him (lapis-blue skin, double plumes, was-sceptre) follows standard Egyptian iconography. The tunnel genius Kurgasiax is the Liber 231 genius of Kaph, which Kenneth Grant used as the name for the Tunnel of Set in Nightside of Eden.

rows.title: The Path of the Balance
rows.summary: Path 22 joins Tiphareth, the solar heart of the Tree, to Geburah, the fiery sphere of Mars. It runs under the letter Lamed (the ox-goad), the sign Libra and Atu VIII Adjustment. Working it builds a felt sense of equilibrium: every act is met by its exact consequence, and Geburah's sword and the scales of Maat belong together. It trains clear judgement without cruelty, and honesty without self-punishment.
rows.prepare_incense: Galbanum, the 777 perfume for Lamed (col. XLII). A little olibanum may be burned at the opening for the Tiphareth temple.
rows.prepare_candle: An emerald-green candle (King scale of path 22) on a blue altar cloth (Queen scale of path 22). A gold or yellow candle for Tiphareth (its Queen scale) is optional.
rows.prepare_stone: Emerald (777 col. XL). Any clear green stone can stand in if you have no emerald.
rows.prepare_facing: East. Libra is a cardinal Air sign, and Golden Dawn practice gives Air to the East. East is also the usual quarter for opening from Tiphareth.
rows.prepare_notes: Best on a Friday or in an hour of Venus (Libra's ruler), or while the Sun or Moon is in Libra. Banish first (LBRP or Star Ruby) and do the Qabalistic Cross. The journey starts in Tiphareth, so it helps to have worked the lower paths into Tiphareth (25, 26, 24) first. Study the Thoth Atu VIII for a few minutes before closing your eyes. Keep your diary and pen within reach, and use a soft timer if you are not being read to.
rows.closing: Once you are back in the room, perform the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram (or the Star Ruby, if that is your practice) and seal with the Qabalistic Cross. Stamp your feet, drink water and eat something plain. In your magical diary, record the date, time, planetary hour and the Moon's sign, the guide's word or symbol, and everything you saw. Then check it against the symbol list. Note what matched, what did not, and anything that felt imposed rather than received. Leave interpretation for a day or two.
rows.tunnel_reflection: The averse face of Lamed is the tampered scale. It is judgement that has lost its measure, karma imagined as revenge, and the sword used to settle scores rather than to adjust. Consider where your own sense of balance hardens into punishment, of others or of yourself, and where 'justice' has become a mask for resentment. Hold this as a question to look at in daylight, not a current to call up. Work the day-side path of Adjustment first, until true equilibrium is familiar enough that you can recognise its distortion.
rows.notes: Thoth attribution: Lamed, Libra, Atu VIII Adjustment. The digest's 'atu XI' is the Golden Dawn numbering. The Golden Dawn put Justice at XI and Strength at VIII so the numbers followed the letter order. Crowley kept the letter and sign attributions but went back to the older numbering: Adjustment VIII, Lust XI. This is only a renumbering. It is not the He/Tzaddi swap, which affects paths 15 and 28. Corrections to the digest: (1) Greek gods: 777 gives Themis, Minos, Aeacus and Rhadamanthus for Lamed. The digest split this list across paths 21 and 22 because of a row shift. (2) Trump title: 777's full title for this trump is 'The Daughter of the Lords of Truth; the Ruler of the Balance'. Its first half had shifted into path 21's row. (3) Magical weapon: only the Cross of Equilibrium belongs to Lamed. 'The Cup and Cross of Suffering' is Mem's (path 23) and spilled into this row, as did 'The Hanged Man—[Cups]' in the general tarot attribution. (4) The digest's 'Divine name of the path: אל' is not used. It is probably another row shift: El is the divine name of Jupiter and Chesed, so it would belong to Kaph (path 21), while 777 usually gives the zodiacal paths permutations of YHVH. This could not be confirmed against the table. Geburah's God-name, seen at the threshold, is אלהים גבור, Elohim Gibor. Reading AL as the ox (Aleph) plus the goad (Lamed), with Adjustment as the Fool's complement, is Crowley's own Thelemic interpretation, not an older tradition. The Sepher Yetzirah text is paraphrased. The tunnel genius Lafcursiax is the Liber 231 genius of Lamed, which Kenneth Grant used as the name for the Tunnel of Set in Nightside of Eden.

rows.title: The Path of the Still Deep
rows.summary: The 23rd path runs straight up the Pillar of Severity from Hod, the sphere of Mercury and the analytical mind, to Geburah, the sphere of Mars and just force, through Mem, the Mother letter of Water, and Atu XII, the Hanged Man. The Sepher Yetzirah calls it the Stable Intelligence, and it teaches the intellect to suspend itself: to be turned upside down and held steady by something deeper than its own cleverness. Working it builds surrender without collapse, and a calm that can meet severity without being swept away.
rows.prepare_incense: Onycha and myrrh (777 col. XLII). Onycha is hard to find; myrrh alone, or myrrh with a little storax (Hod's perfume), will do.
rows.prepare_candle: A deep blue candle (the path's King scale, 777 col. XV) on a sea-green cloth (the path's Queen scale, col. XVI). An orange light for the Hod temple (Hod's Queen scale) is optional.
rows.prepare_stone: Beryl or aquamarine (777 col. XL)
rows.prepare_facing: West, the quarter of Water in the Golden Dawn and Pentagram-ritual arrangement
rows.prepare_notes: Set a cup of clean water or wine on the altar; 777 gives the path's weapon as the Cup and Cross of Suffering, and Wine. Banish before you begin (Star Ruby or LBRP). Any time is suitable, and some prefer the Moon in a water sign. Keep a journal and pen within reach. If water or inversion imagery distresses you, keep the causeway firm under your feet and skip the optional sharing of the Hanged Man's view in step 7.
rows.closing: Banish with the Star Ruby or the LBRP. Stamp firmly on the floor and put out the candle. Pour the water away with a word of thanks, or drink the wine. Eat something warm and solid, and wash your hands and face. Record the working right away: date, time, conditions, the vision in order, the word or symbol from Asar, and any bodily sensations, especially in the belly. Afterwards, check your record against the symbol list. Mark what matched, what did not and what surprised you, without revising the vision. Note your dreams for the next few nights.
rows.tunnel_reflection: In the averse aspect the waters stop being a medium of surrender and become a place to disappear: passivity that calls itself acceptance, a mind that has given up its shape instead of offering it. Consider where you may have mistaken stagnation for peace or martyrdom for devotion, and where the Hanged Man's stillness has become a way of never acting. Treat this as contemplation after the day-side path has been worked and grounded, not as a working to enter or invoke.
rows.notes: This journey uses Crowley's Thoth/777 attributions. The He/Tzaddi swap does not affect this path, and the Golden Dawn and Thoth attributions agree: Mem, Water, Atu XII The Hanged Man. Mem is one of the three Mother letters (Aleph, Mem, Shin) of the Sepher Yetzirah. Digest corrections: (1) Hod's God-name was misspelled אלהים בצאות; the correct form is אלהים צבאות, Elohim Tzabaoth. (2) Hod's heaven was misspelled כובכ; the correct form is כוכב, Kokab. (3) The digest gives the letter name as מים 'Maim'. That is the word for water, which is the letter's meaning, and a spelling carried in 777-derived tables. The standard spelling of the letter's name is מם, Mem, and that is the name traced and vibrated here. (4) The trump-title field ran into Atu XIII's title. Atu XII is 'The Spirit of the Mighty Waters'; 'The Child of the Great Transformers' belongs to Death. (5) Geburah's vision field was merged with Tiphareth's. Geburah's vision is 'The Vision of Power'; the Vision of the Harmony of Things belongs to Tiphareth. (6) 777 gives this row's magical weapon as 'Cup and Cross of Suffering, Wine'; the digest listed only Wine [Water of Lustration]. (7) 'Queens' in the general Tarot attribution means the four Queens, the court cards of Water grouped with this row in 777 col. XIV; the trump itself is Atu XII. Mikael is Hod's archangel in the Golden Dawn/777 order; some writers swap Mikael and Raphael between Hod and Tiphareth. The guide step includes the Golden Dawn habit of testing a figure by tracing the path's letter before it; this is optional, and it comes before accepting the cup. In The Book of Thoth, Crowley treats the Hanged Man's formula of redemptive sacrifice as belonging mainly to the Old Aeon of Osiris. In Thelemic work the path can be approached as surrendering the ego's control to the deeper Will rather than as sacrifice for its own sake. The Thoth card details (ankh, crossed legs over a triangle, green tablets, nails, serpent below) are described in original words.

rows.title: The Path of the Scythe and the Scarab
rows.summary: The 24th path joins Netzach, the sphere of Venus and the feelings, to Tiphareth, the solar centre of the self, through the letter Nun (Fish), the sign Scorpio and Atu XIII, Death. The Sepher Yetzirah calls it the Imaginative Intelligence: here the forms the heart has clung to break down so that their essence can pass upward into the Sun. Working it builds the ability to let things end without losing what lived in them, and a steadier relationship with change, decay and renewal.
rows.prepare_incense: Siamese benzoin and opoponax (777 col. XLII). For the Netzach temple you can open with Netzach's own perfume of benzoin, rose and red sandalwood.
rows.prepare_candle: A green-blue candle (the path's King scale, 777 col. XV) on a dull brown cloth (the path's Queen scale, col. XVI). An emerald-green light for the Netzach temple (Netzach's Queen scale) is optional.
rows.prepare_stone: Snakestone, for which an ammonite fossil serves, or greenish turquoise (777 col. XL)
rows.prepare_facing: West. Scorpio is fixed Water, and West is the quarter of Water (the Eagle Kerub) in the Golden Dawn and Pentagram-ritual arrangement. If your temple has a fixed orientation, East is an acceptable default.
rows.prepare_notes: Banish before you begin (Star Ruby or LBRP). A Tuesday (Mars, traditional ruler of Scorpio) or a time with the Moon in Scorpio suits this path, but timing is optional. 777 gives this path the magical weapon 'The Pain of the Obligation' [The Oath], so you may quietly restate your own oath or aspiration before you start. Keep a journal and pen within reach. This path deals with endings and decay. Postpone it during a raw bereavement or a hard low period.
rows.closing: Perform the Star Ruby or the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram. Stamp your foot firmly on the floor and put out the candle. Eat and drink something substantial, such as bread and something salty, and wash your hands and face in cool water. Write up the working right away: date, time, astrological conditions, what you saw, heard and felt in order, Khephra's word or symbol, and anything unexpected. Only then check your record against the symbol list. Mark honestly what matched, what did not and what surprised you, and do not edit the vision to fit. Note your dreams for the next few nights.
rows.tunnel_reflection: On the night side the same letter becomes a stagnant pool: decay that feeds nothing, and a fascination with endings that curls back on itself like the scorpion turning its sting on its own body. Consider where in you grief, resentment or morbid fascination has stopped composting and started simply to rot, and what it would take to let it move again. Hold this as reflection only, after the day-side path has been worked and grounded. It is not a place to enter or invoke.
rows.notes: This journey uses Crowley's Thoth/777 attributions throughout. The He/Tzaddi swap affects only paths 15 and 28, and the Golden Dawn and Thoth attributions agree here: Nun, Scorpio, Atu XIII Death. Digest corrections: (1) The animal list read 'Scorpio'. 777 col. XXXVIII gives 'Scorpion, Beetle, Lobster or Crayfish, [Wolf]'. (2) The trump-title field ran into the next row. 'The Daughter of the Reconcilers' is the title of Atu XIV (Art/Temperance). Atu XIII is 'The Child of the Great Transformers; the Lord of the Gate of Death'. (3) Tiphareth's vision field was truncated. 777 gives 'The Vision of the Harmony of Things (also the Mysteries of the Crucifixion)', and the digest's bracketed 'Beatific Vision' is a supplementary attribution. Haniel is spelled האניאל as in 777; הניאל is also common. Raphael is Tiphareth's archangel in the Golden Dawn/777 order used here; some later writers swap Raphael and Michael between Tiphareth and Hod. Khephra is the guide, chosen from 777 col. XIX. He fits the path's beetle and its Empress-scale colour 'like a black beetle', and he echoes the Sun of Tiphareth. Typhon and Apep, from the same list, belong more to the averse side. The guide step includes the Golden Dawn habit of testing a figure by tracing the path's letter before it; this is optional. The Thoth card details (Osirian crown, bubbles of new forms, scorpion/serpent/eagle, fish) are described in original words. Snakestone is commonly taken to mean an ammonite fossil.

rows.title: The Arrow through the Rainbow
rows.summary: Path 25 rises straight up the Middle Pillar from Yesod, the Moon's foundation of images, to Tiphareth, the solar centre, by way of Samekh (the Prop), Sagittarius and Atu XIV Art. It is the path of the arrow loosed from the rainbow's bow, and of the alchemical cauldron where fire and water mix into something new. Working it builds single-pointed aspiration, steadiness under testing, and the art of blending your own opposites into a third thing.
rows.prepare_incense: Lign-aloes (777 col. XLII), i.e. agarwood or oud. Jasmine, Yesod's perfume, suits the opening temple.
rows.prepare_candle: Blue (King scale, the path's own colour), or yellow (Queen scale) instead. A violet cloth or candle (Yesod, Queen scale) for the temple you start from.
rows.prepare_stone: Jacinth (777 col. XL). An orange-red zircon or hessonite is the usual modern stand-in.
rows.prepare_facing: South, the quarter of Fire (Sagittarius is mutable Fire), or East if your temple is always set up that way.
rows.prepare_notes: Thursday (Jupiter rules Sagittarius) or Monday (the Moon, for Yesod) suit this working; some practitioners also choose a time when the Sun or Moon is in Sagittarius. Keep Atu XIV in view and study it beforehand. This is one of the three Golden Dawn Portal paths (24, 25, 26), usually worked after paths 32 to 27. It climbs the Middle Pillar directly and crosses the Veil of Paroketh. Allow 30 to 40 minutes including reading time, and keep a journal within reach.
rows.closing: Close with a banishing: the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram, or the Star Ruby (Liber XXV). Stamp your feet, wash your hands and face, and eat and drink something plain and grounding. Write up the journey at once: date, time, planetary hour, incense, what you saw, what the figure of Art said or gave you, bodily sensations and mood. Check the record against the symbol list below. Note which correspondences turned up without prompting, which did not, and anything that clashed with them. Over the next days, add any theme of tempering, testing or aim that surfaces in dreams or daily life.
rows.tunnel_reflection: The averse face of Samekh is failed alchemy: fire and water forced together before their time, poison where there should be elixir, an arrow loosed without aim that falls short in the desert. Consider where you have mixed things that were not ready, or mistaken restlessness for aspiration, and what your arrow still needs before it can fly true. Contemplate this from ordinary waking awareness, as reflection and not invocation, and only after you have worked the day-side path of Samekh and recorded it.
rows.notes: Attributions follow Crowley's Thoth scheme: Samekh, Sagittarius, Atu XIV Art (called 'Temperance' in the Golden Dawn and Rider-Waite decks), joining Yesod (9) to Tiphareth (6) on the Middle Pillar. The Liber AL I:57 He/Tzaddi (Star/Emperor) exchange does not affect this path. Corrections to the digest: (1) 'Temperence' is spelled Temperance. (2) The trump title was cut short; the full 777 / Golden Dawn title is 'The Daughter of the Reconcilers, the Bringer-forth of Life'. (3) Yesod's grade was given as '2°=9□ Theoricus 1°=10□ Zelator'. That is a shifted row: Yesod is 2°=9□ Theoricus only, and 1°=10□ Zelator belongs to Malkuth. (4) Yesod's perfume 'Jinseng' is the spelling 777 itself uses; it means ginseng. The digest's 'complete practical attribution of Egyptian gods' field is in Coptic script (read as Arōueris, Horus the Elder). Its reading is uncertain, so the script does not use it. Archangels follow the Golden Dawn / 777 order (Gabriel in Yesod, Raphael in Tiphareth). Temples use the Queen scale (Yesod violet, Tiphareth gold), and the letter is traced in the path's King-scale blue. The rainbow-as-bow image comes from the Golden Dawn teaching that Qoph, Shin and Tau (paths 29, 31, 32) spell Qesheth, the bow, from which Samekh's arrow is loosed toward Tiphareth through the Veil of Paroketh. The jacinth arrowhead, the centaur handing over the arrow and the desert of testing are working images, not traditional doctrine. The digest's 'keyword' and 'meditation' lines are the app's editorial synthesis and are not presented as tradition. The tunnel genius Saksaksalim follows Kenneth Grant's Nightside of Eden (Liber 231).

rows.title: The Path of the Opened Eye
rows.summary: Path 26 joins Hod, the Splendour of the mind, to Tiphareth, the solar heart of the Tree, by way of Ayin (the Eye), Capricorn and Atu XV The Devil. It is the climb up the mountain of matter in the company of Pan. Working it trains you to see through fixed appearances and the chains you mistake for reality, and to meet raw creative and instinctual force with clear sight and laughter instead of fear or shame.
rows.prepare_incense: Musk or civet (777 col. XLII, which also allows Saturnian perfumes). Use synthetic musk or ambrette seed, not animal products. Storax, Hod's perfume, suits the opening temple.
rows.prepare_candle: Indigo (King scale, the path's own colour) or black (Queen scale) for the path. An orange candle or cloth (Hod, Queen scale) for the temple you start from.
rows.prepare_stone: Black diamond (777 col. XL). Any dark faceted stone can stand in as a focus.
rows.prepare_facing: North, the quarter of Earth (Capricorn is cardinal Earth), or East if your temple is always set up that way.
rows.prepare_notes: Saturday (Saturn rules Capricorn) or Wednesday (Mercury, for Hod) suit this working; some practitioners also choose a time when the Sun or Moon is in Capricorn. Keep Atu XV in view and study it before you begin. In the Golden Dawn this is one of the three Portal paths (24, 25, 26), usually worked after paths 32 to 27. Allow 30 to 40 minutes including reading time, and keep a journal and pen within reach.
rows.closing: Close with a banishing: the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram, or the Star Ruby. Stamp your feet, wash your hands and face in cool water, and eat and drink something simple and grounding, like bread and a warm drink. Then write up the journey straight away: date, time, planetary hour, incense, what you saw, the word or symbol Pan gave you, bodily sensations and mood. Check the record against the symbol list below. Note which correspondences appeared without prompting, which did not, and anything that contradicted them. Come back to the entry after a few days and add anything that has surfaced since in dreams or daily life.
rows.tunnel_reflection: On the averse side the Eye stops looking upward. Matter is taken as the whole, the goat has no eye above its horns, and the chain is mistaken for the body. Consider where a fixed appearance has become a prison in your own life, and where laughter has soured into contempt. Hold this as quiet reflection from ordinary waking awareness, not as invocation, and only after you have worked the day-side path of Ayin and written up what it taught you.
rows.notes: Attributions follow Crowley's Thoth scheme: Ayin, Capricorn, Atu XV The Devil, joining Hod (8) to Tiphareth (6). The Liber AL I:57 He/Tzaddi (Star/Emperor) exchange does not affect this path; the Golden Dawn and the Thoth deck agree on it. Corrections to the digest: (1) Hod's God-name was given as אלהים בצאות, with letters transposed. It is corrected to אלהים צבאות, Elohim Tzabaoth. (2) Hod's Heaven was given as כובכ and is corrected to כוכב, Kokab. Archangels follow the Golden Dawn / 777 order (Mikael in Hod, Raphael in Tiphareth). Some modern writers swap these two; if your lineage does, change the archangel in step 2. Temples use the Queen scale (Hod orange, Tiphareth gold), and the letter is traced in the path's King-scale indigo. 'Khem' is the older reading of Min, the ithyphallic god of Koptos, which 777 pairs with Set. The path crosses the Veil of Paroketh, so Tiphareth is glimpsed but not entered. The digest's 'keyword' and 'meditation' lines are the app's own editorial synthesis, and the script does not present them as tradition. The goat's horizontal pupil and the lamp handed over at the veil are working images, not traditional doctrine. The tunnel genius A'ano'nin follows Kenneth Grant's Nightside of Eden (Liber 231). Musk and civet in 777 are animal-derived, so synthetic substitutes are recommended.

rows.title: The Path of the Lightning and the Mouth
rows.summary: Path 27 is the lowest of the Tree's three horizontal paths. It crosses from Hod, the sphere of Mercury and ordered thought, to Netzach, the sphere of Venus and feeling, and carries Pe, the mouth, with Mars and Atu XVI The Tower. Working it builds the courage to let rigid structures of mind break under a greater force, and to meet that breaking as release rather than catastrophe.
rows.prepare_incense: Dragon's blood resin (777 col. XLII, Mars row: 'Pepper, Dragon's Blood, all Hot Pungent Odours'). Burn a few grains of storax first to open the temple of Hod. Do not burn pepper indoors, because the smoke irritates the lungs; set a small dish of whole peppercorns on the altar instead.
rows.prepare_candle: A scarlet candle (King scale of Pe / Mars, 777 col. XV). You can put an orange cloth (Queen scale of Hod, the starting temple) under it.
rows.prepare_stone: Ruby, or any red stone such as garnet or red jasper (777 col. XL).
rows.prepare_facing: East, as in ordinary temple work. South, the quarter of fire, is a fitting alternative for Mars.
rows.prepare_notes: Tuesday (Mars) is the traditional day; Wednesday (Mercury) also suits the start in Hod. A sword or dagger on the altar fits this path (777 col. XLI, The Sword) but is not required. This path can stir up strong feeling, so work it when you are rested and not already upset, and keep your journal ready.
rows.closing: Close with the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram or the Star Ruby, and stamp your foot firmly three times. Because this is a Mars path, work off any leftover energy physically before you sit quietly: a brisk walk, some stretching, or some honest physical work. Eat something substantial and drink water. Record the session at once: the date, time, planetary day and hour, what you saw at the tower, the guide's form and gift, and any emotions it stirred. Check your record against the symbols list only afterwards. If agitation lingers over the following days, don't repeat the path until it settles.
rows.tunnel_reflection: The averse face of Pe is destruction that clears nothing: force spent for its own sake, the tower left as rubble with no new sight in its place, and a mouth that speaks only to wound. Consider how the same lightning that frees can, without the opened eye behind it, become mere rage or a habit of tearing things down. Look honestly at where anger or harsh speech in your own life breaks things without renewing them. Work the day-side path of the Tower first, until you know its shattering as release, and treat Parfaxitas as a theme for reflection and journal work, not a force to call.
rows.notes: ATTRIBUTION: Pe, פה (mouth), value 80 (final ף = 800); Mars; Atu XVI, called The Tower in the Thoth deck and The House of God in the Golden Dawn and 777. Its Golden Dawn title is 'The Lord of the Hosts of the Mighty'. The Thoth swap does not affect this path. Sepher Yetzirah: the 27th path, the Exciting (or Active) Intelligence. Path 27 crosses path 25 (Samekh, Yesod-Tiphareth) on the Middle Pillar, between Yesod and Tiphareth, which is why the journey passes a crossing road. DATA CORRECTIONS: (1) The digest gave Hod's God-name as 'אלהים בצאות', with letters transposed; the correct spelling is אלהים צבאות, Elohim Tzabaoth. (2) The Heavens of Hod appeared as 'כובכ'; the correct form is כוכב, Kokab (Mercury). (3) 777 gives the Empress-scale colour of Pe as 'bright red, rayed azure or emerald', not 'azure or orange'. (4) The trump-title field ran on into the Star's title ('The Daughter of the Firmament...'), apparently from a shifted row; the Tower's title is only 'The Lord of the Hosts of the Mighty'. ARCHANGEL: Mikael for Hod follows the Golden Dawn / 777 order used in this series; some writers swap Mikael and Raphael between Hod and Tiphareth. GUIDE: The falcon-headed guide draws on 777 cols. XIX (Horus) and XX (Menthu); Ares or Mars (cols. XXXIV-XXXV) may appear instead, and you can record whichever form you meet. The remark that the dove and the lion-headed serpent are 'two forms of desire' reports Crowley's reading of the Thoth card; it is not presented as independent tradition.

rows.title: The Path of the Hook and the Throne
rows.summary: Path 28 joins Yesod, the lunar foundation, to Netzach, the sphere of Venus. In Crowley's Thoth attribution it carries Tzaddi, the fish-hook, with Atu IV The Emperor and Aries, the first fire of the zodiac. Working it builds initiative and self-rule: the power to draw the loose tides of imagination up into a clear, living will.
rows.prepare_incense: Dragon's blood resin (777 col. XLII, Aries row 15; the Thoth swap brings Aries' correspondences to Tzaddi). You can burn a little jasmine first to open the lunar temple of Yesod. Golden Dawn users would burn galbanum (Aquarius) here instead.
rows.prepare_candle: A scarlet candle (King scale of Aries, 777 col. XV, row 15, which the Thoth swap brings to Tzaddi) on a violet cloth (Queen scale of Yesod, the starting temple). Golden Dawn alternative: violet, the King scale of Aquarius.
rows.prepare_stone: Ruby (777 col. XL, Aries row). A garnet or other clear red stone will do if you have no ruby.
rows.prepare_facing: East, toward sunrise. This suits Aries, the sign of the spring equinox and of the Sun's exaltation.
rows.prepare_notes: This working is especially apt with the Sun in Aries (around the spring equinox and the Thelemic Equinox of the Gods), on a Tuesday (Mars rules Aries), or on a Monday for the start in Yesod. Keep your journal and pen within reach, and make sure you will not be disturbed for about 30 minutes.
rows.closing: Close with the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram or the Star Ruby, then stamp the floor three times to seal. Eat and drink something simple (bread, fruit, water) and wash your hands and face. Write your journal record at once: the date, time, Moon phase and the Sun's sign, what appeared on the path, anything that didn't match what you expected, and the Emperor's word or symbol exactly as it came. Compare it with the symbols checklist only after writing. Note whether the images matched the Aries (Thoth) set or the Aquarius (Golden Dawn) set; that tells you something about which attribution your own imagery follows.
rows.tunnel_reflection: In its averse aspect, the path of Tzaddi shows authority cut off from the life it was meant to serve: rule that feeds only itself, a hook that catches and holds but never draws anything up into the light. Without calling on anything, contemplate where your own will has hardened into mere control, or where a rigid inner law keeps your imagination captive. Work the day-side path of the Emperor several times, until you know it well, before taking up this reflection. Treat the tunnel as a subject for meditation and journal study, not as an invocation.
rows.notes: ATTRIBUTION: Crowley's Thoth swap (Liber AL I:57, 'but צ is not the Star', i.e. Tzaddi; explained in The Book of Thoth) gives Tzaddi to Atu IV The Emperor and He to Atu XVII The Star. The paths follow their letters, so in the Thoth system path 28 (Tzaddi, Netzach-Yesod) carries The Emperor / Aries, and path 15 (He, Chokmah-Tiphareth) carries The Star / Aquarius. In the Golden Dawn attribution, and in the rows of 777 as printed, path 28 is Atu XVII The Star / Aquarius, titled 'Daughter of the Firmament, Dweller between the Waters'. DATA CORRECTIONS: The digest lists the Golden Dawn / Aquarius set for this path: The Star, Atu XVII; Aquarius; King scale violet, Queen sky blue, Emperor bluish mauve, Empress white tinged purple; galbanum; man or eagle and peacock; olive and coconut; artificial glass; Ahephi, Aroueris and Nuit; Athena and Ganymede; Juno; Astrology. Under the Thoth swap the sign's correspondences go with the trump, so this journey uses 777's Aries row (row 15) instead: King scale scarlet, Queen red, Emperor brilliant flame, Empress glowing red; ram and owl; tiger lily and geranium; ruby; dragon's blood; the horns, energy and burin; Men Thu, Athena, Mars/Minerva, Shiva; the power of consecrating things; head and face. The digest's trump title ('Dweller between the Waters') and trump design ('a water-nymph') belong to the Star; the Emperor's Golden Dawn title is 'Sun of the Morning, Chief among the Mighty'. The digest's magical-weapons field ('The Censer or Aspergillus The Twilight of the Place and Magic') appears to merge two rows. Some things stay with the path whichever attribution you use: the letter Tzaddi צדי (fish-hook), value 90 (final ץ = 900), its position between Netzach and Yesod, and the 28th Sepher Yetzirah path, the Natural Intelligence. The digest spells Haniel האניאל; the usual spelling is הניאל. The tunnel digest pairs Tzuflifu with the Emperor / Aries (Crowley/Grant) and gives the Golden Dawn Star / Aquarius as the alternative. VARIANT: If you keep path colours with the letter rather than the sign, trace Tzaddi in violet instead of scarlet. Nothing else in the working needs to change.

rows.title: The Path Between the Towers
rows.summary: Path 29 runs from Malkuth, the Kingdom of the physical world, to Netzach, the Victory of feeling and desire. It is governed by Qoph (the back of the head), Pisces and Atu XVIII The Moon. It is the Corporeal Intelligence: the road through the body's instincts, fears and dreams, where the Sun travels unseen through the night before it rises. Working it builds the ability to walk through illusion and fear without running from it or believing it, and to trust the slow, patient life of the body.
rows.prepare_incense: Ambergris (777 col. XLII). Real ambergris is rare; an ambergris-type blend or ambrette seed will do as a stand-in. Note the substitution in your record.
rows.prepare_candle: A deep crimson candle (King scale, 'crimson, ultra violet') on a buff or stone-coloured cloth (Queen and Empress scales).
rows.prepare_stone: Pearl (777 col. XL).
rows.prepare_facing: West, the quarter of Water, since Pisces is mutable Water. In the vision the temple of Malkuth faces east, and the Qoph door is right of centre (south-east), with the Tree seen from the front.
rows.prepare_notes: Best worked at night, and a waning moon suits it: Crowley's correct design for this trump is the waning moon. Work barefoot, because the path rules the legs and feet. A small hand mirror (the path's weapon) and a bowl of water can sit on the altar. Study Atu XVIII for a few minutes beforehand. This path stirs fear and glamour, so choose a time when you are rested and steady, and do not skip the banishing afterwards.
rows.closing: Close with the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram or your usual banishing. This path works with illusion and glamour, so do not leave the banishing out. Put out the candle and switch on an ordinary light. Write the record at once, describing what you saw before you interpret it. Then test it against the symbol list and note what matched, what did not, and anything new. Eat something substantial, drink water, and wash your hands and face in cold water. Because this path touches the dreaming mind, give your dreams a line in the journal for the next few nights. Leave at least a day before working another path.
rows.tunnel_reflection: The averse side of Qoph is the Moon's tide turned to nightmare. It is illusion taken for revelation, glamour that bewitches the one who casts it, fear rising from the oldest part of the brain, and a road that keeps doubling back on itself. Consider where you have been deceived by your own images, or where fear has quietly steered your choices while calling itself caution or intuition. Keep Qulielfi's tunnel as a subject for reflection and journal work, never as something to call up, and turn to it only after you have walked and recorded the day-side path of Qoph with a clear, banished mind.
rows.notes: Attributions follow Crowley's Thoth system and Liber 777: Qoph (value 100, 'back of the head'), Pisces, Atu XVIII The Moon, titled 'The Ruler of Flux and Reflux, the Child of the Sons of the Mighty', running from Malkuth to Netzach. Crowley's correct design for the trump is the waning moon. The He/Tzaddi exchange of paths 15 and 28 does not affect this path. Corrections to the digest: (1) Malkuth's Hebrew name was misspelt מלכור and is corrected to מלכות. (2) 777 gives Malkuth's magical image as 'a young woman, crowned and throned', not 'veiled'. (3) The col. V entry '(36) אלה' (Eloh) is the Sun's name, shifted from path 30, and is not used here. On the God-name: 777 gives Adonai Melekh (אדני מלך), while Golden Dawn practice often uses Adonai ha-Aretz (אדני הארץ). Vibrate whichever one you use in your own Malkuth work. 777 spells Haniel as האניאל; הניאל is the more usual spelling. Opium is one of 777's plants for this path; here it appears only as imagery. The double-bracketed perfume in the digest is left out of the practical preparation. Linking Pisces to Netzach through Venus's exaltation in Pisces is standard astrology used as imagery, not a 777 entry. Directions assume you see the Tree from the front while facing east, which puts Netzach on the right. Mirror them if you use the body convention.

rows.title: The Path of the Unwalled Sky
