rows.summary: Path 30 joins Yesod, the Foundation of images and dreams, to Hod, the Splendour of mind and language. It runs under the letter Resh (the head or face), the Sun and Atu XIX The Sun. It is the Collecting Intelligence, where scattered impressions are gathered into ordered knowledge and the intellect is lit from above instead of by its own reflections. Working it builds clarity, honesty about what one actually knows, and a warm confidence that does not need to guard itself.
rows.prepare_incense: Olibanum (frankincense) with a little cinnamon (777 col. XLII, 'all glorious odours').
rows.prepare_candle: An orange candle (King scale, the path's own colour) on a gold-yellow cloth (Queen scale). A small violet light for Yesod is optional.
rows.prepare_stone: Chrysolite (777 col. XL). The old name covers yellow-green stones such as peridot. If you have none, a clear sunny stone can stand in; note the substitution in your record.
rows.prepare_facing: East, toward sunrise. In the vision the temple of Yesod also faces east, and the Resh door is in the left-hand (north-east) wall, with the Tree seen from the front.
rows.prepare_notes: Best worked by day, ideally on a Sunday or in the Sun's planetary hour. Before you begin, spend a few minutes studying Atu XIX where you can see it. Keep your journal and pen within reach. A bay (laurel) leaf, sunflower seeds, or a small image of a lion or hawk can sit on the altar. Keep the room warm and well aired.
rows.closing: Close with the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram or your usual banishing, then put out the candle. Write the record straight away: the date and time, and every image, word and sensation, including the guide's answer. Describe what happened before you interpret it. Afterwards, check the record against the symbol list and note what matched, what did not, and anything new. Eat something simple and drink water. Step out into daylight if you can. Leave at least a day before working another path.
rows.tunnel_reflection: The averse side of Resh is the Sun as glare instead of light. It is brilliance that blinds rather than shows, vanity, false enlightenment, and a bright face with nothing behind it. Consider where in your own life you have mistaken being seen for seeing, or confidence for clarity. Keep Raflifu's tunnel as a subject for reflection and journal work, not as something to call up, and turn to it only after you have worked and recorded the day-side path of Resh.
rows.notes: Attributions follow Crowley's Thoth system and Liber 777: Resh (value 200, 'head'), the Sun, Atu XIX The Sun, titled 'The Lord of the Fire of the World', running from Yesod to Hod. The He/Tzaddi exchange of paths 15 and 28 does not affect this path. Corrections to the digest: (1) Hod's God-name was misspelt אלהים בצאות and is corrected to אלהים צבאות, Elohim Tzabaoth. (2) Hod's heaven כובכ is corrected to כוכב, Kokab. (3) The 777 col. V entry seems shifted by one row. אלהים (Elohim) is the divine name of Fire and belongs to path 31. The Sun's name is אלה (Eloh, value 36, the number of cells in the 6x6 square of the Sun), which the digest places on path 29. (4) Several fields have path 31 (Fire / Atu XX, titled The Aeon in the Thoth deck) material mixed in, and it was not used here: 'The Angel or Last Judgement' in the Tarot field; Thoum-Aesh-Neith, Mau and Kabeshunt among the Egyptian gods; Agni and Yama among the Hindu deities (777 gives Surya for the Sun); and 'the Wand or Lamp, Pyramid of Fire' among the weapons (the Sun's are the Lamen or Bow and Arrow). Directions assume you see the Tree from the front while facing east, which puts Hod on the left. If you use the 'backed into the Tree' body convention, mirror them. The guide is Ra, following 777 cols. XIX-XX. Some Thelemites will meet Ra-Hoor-Khuit here; that is a personal reading, not the table's attribution.

rows.title: The Path of the Primal Fire
rows.summary: Path 31, Shin, joins Malkuth to Hod on the Pillar of Severity. It carries elemental Fire and, in its second attribution, Spirit. Crowley's Atu XX, The Aeon, replaces the old Judgement with the gods of the Stele of Revealing and marks the passing of one age into the next. Working it develops the ability to let the fire of spirit burn away stale forms in the self, so that resurrection is felt as renewal and not punishment, and it readies the mind for the clarity of Hod.
rows.prepare_incense: Olibanum (frankincense), which 777 col. XLII gives with 'all fiery odours'. Dittany of Crete (Malkuth) may be burned briefly first to establish the temple.
rows.prepare_candle: Glowing orange-scarlet candle (King scale, 777 col. XV) on a vermilion cloth (Queen scale, col. XVI).
rows.prepare_stone: Fire opal (777 col. XL).
rows.prepare_facing: South, the quarter of Fire in the Golden Dawn scheme. Face East instead if you keep a fixed temple orientation for all path work.
rows.prepare_notes: A single steady flame on the altar is the natural focus. You may set red poppies, hibiscus or any scarlet flowers beside it, and a wand if you have one. Place the candle safely and never leave it unattended. Banish beforehand with the LBRP or the Star Ruby. Keep your record book open beside you. If you are working the paths in sequence, work path 32 (Tau) first.
rows.closing: After stamping your feet, close with the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram or the Star Ruby. Put out the candle deliberately, with a snuffer if you have one, as a conscious act of ending the working. Drink cool water and eat something. Write the record at once: date, time, moon phase, planetary day and hour, your physical state, and everything seen, heard or received. Then go through the symbols checklist and note what matched and what did not. Treat unfamiliar images as material to research, not as authority.
rows.tunnel_reflection: Liber 231 names Shalicu as the genius of the tunnel behind Shin. Its averse face is fire that only annihilates: judgement without mercy, and a hunger for apocalypse as an ending instead of a birth, burning down what could have been transformed. Consider where you are drawn toward that kind of destruction, of habits, of relationships or of yourself, and ask what renewal the day-side fire of the Aeon would offer in its place. Work the day-side path first, and hold this as reflection only, never as invocation.
rows.notes: Dual attribution: Shin carries both Fire (path 31) and Spirit (31 bis). 777 gives Spirit its own row: King scale white merging into grey, Queen scale deep purple nearly black, Emperor scale the seven prismatic colours with violet outside, and Empress scale white, red, yellow, blue and black, with black outside. This journey works the Fire aspect, with the spiritual renewal of the Aeon as its theme. Trump: Crowley replaced the Golden Dawn's Atu XX Judgement (an angel with a trumpet and the dead rising) with The Aeon, drawn from the Stele of Revealing, to mark the Aeon of Horus. The 777 'correct design' entry still describes Israfel and the rising dead, and the journey shows the old image giving way to the new. The He/Tzaddi swap does not affect this path. Corrections to the digest: (1) the Hebrew spelling of Malkuth is 'מלכור' in the digest and should be מלכות. (2) Hod's God-name is misspelled 'אלהים בצאות'; it should be אלהים צבאות, Elohim Tzabaoth. (3) The Heavens of Hod are misspelled 'כובכ'; they should be כוכב, Kokab. (4) The magical image of Malkuth is 'a young woman, crowned and throned', not 'veiled'. (5) The digest's col. V divine name for this path, '(15) יה (3) אב', matches the Saturn magic-square names (Ab = 3, Yah = 15). It appears to be a row shifted from path 32. The Golden Dawn elemental God-name of Fire is Elohim (אלהים). (6) The Hindu entry 'Surya (as ☉)' looks shifted from path 30 (the Sun). For this path 777 gives Agni (Tejas), the fire god, together with Yama, lord and judge of the dead; verify this against your edition. (7) In the grade column, Malkuth is 1°=10□, not 0°=0□. The digest's Hod grade of 3°=8□ Practicus is correct in both the Golden Dawn and the A∴A∴. The Hod temple details are kept to its standard attributions: orange (Queen scale), the hermaphrodite image, Elohim Tzabaoth, and Mikael.

rows.title: The Path into the Night of Time
rows.summary: Path 32, Tau, runs from Malkuth straight up the Middle Pillar to Yesod. It is attributed to Saturn and to Earth, and its trump is Atu XXI, The Universe. It is traditionally the first path worked upward. It trains the passage from bodily, sensory awareness into the astral Foundation and back again, and it teaches Saturn's lessons of patience, limit and form, with the finished world seen as a completion and not a prison.
rows.prepare_incense: 777 col. XLII gives assafoetida, scammony, indigo and sulphur ('all evil odours'). These are unpleasant and impractical to burn indoors. Burn Dittany of Crete (Malkuth), myrrh (Binah, the Sephirah of Saturn) or storax (777's perfume for the Earth attribution) instead.
rows.prepare_candle: Indigo candle (King scale, 777 col. XV) on a black cloth (Queen scale, col. XVI). A black candle is also acceptable.
rows.prepare_stone: Onyx (777 col. XL). You can also place a small dish of salt on the altar for the Earth attribution (32 bis).
rows.prepare_facing: East, toward the imagined veils of the Tree. North, the Golden Dawn quarter of Earth, also suits this path.
rows.prepare_notes: Saturday or an hour of Saturn suits the path. Work in dim light. Tau is the usual first path in a pathworking sequence because it leaves Malkuth by the Middle Pillar. Banish beforehand with the LBRP or the Star Ruby. Keep your magical record open beside you so you can write immediately afterward.
rows.closing: Once you have stamped your feet and are fully back, close the working with the Lesser Banishing Ritual of the Pentagram or the Star Ruby. Eat something plain and earthy (bread with a little salt suits this path) and drink water. Write your record at once: date, time, moon phase, planetary day and hour, how your body felt, and everything you saw, heard or received, however small. Then go through the symbols checklist and note what matched. Treat anything that appeared but is not in the correspondences as a question to research, not a revelation to accept.
rows.tunnel_reflection: Liber 231 names Thantifaxath as the genius of the tunnel behind Tau. Its averse face is matter felt as a tomb: form as nothing but imprisonment, time as nothing but loss, and the finished world as a dead end where there should be a dance. Notice where that mood lives in you, in routines that have hardened or in a body felt only as a burden, and set the day-side image of the dancing maiden against it. Work the day-side path until it is familiar before you turn to its shadow, and hold this only as a meditation, never as a call to the genius.
rows.notes: Dual attribution: Tau carries both Saturn (path 32) and Earth (32 bis), and 777 gives Earth its own row. That row has a King scale of citrine, olive, russet and black, a Queen scale of amber, the stone salt, and the divine name Adonai ha-Aretz (אדני הארץ). The digest's col. V entry for this path, '[הארץ]אדני', is that Earth name. This journey works the Saturnian path, and Earth is present through the Malkuth temple and the dish of salt. You may vibrate Adonai ha-Aretz in place of Adonai Melekh; both are standard names of Malkuth. Atu XXI is 'The Universe' in both the Golden Dawn and Thoth decks, so the He/Tzaddi swap does not affect this path. The descriptions of the trump are drawn from Crowley's Thoth design: the dancing maiden with the serpent, the ellipse of 72 circles, the Kerubim, and the house of the elements at the base. Corrections to the digest: (1) the Hebrew spelling of Malkuth is 'מלכור' in the digest and should be מלכות. (2) The magical image of Malkuth in 777 and Golden Dawn is 'a young woman, crowned and throned', not 'veiled'. (3) The grade column appears shifted. Malkuth is 1°=10□ (Zelator in the Golden Dawn, Neophyte in the A∴A∴), 0°=0□ lies outside the Tree, and Yesod is 2°=9□ alone. (4) The Saturn divine names from the magic square, Ab (אב, 3) and Yah (יה, 15), appear in the digest under path 31. They belong with this path's Saturn attribution. The 777 'evil odours' incense is listed for completeness but substitutes are recommended.
